# mmx diagram conversation

## In pi

The pi-mmx extension runs the mmx routine for you:

- Before each run it collects the human's unanswered turns for every tracked
  diagram and injects them as an `mmx-turn` message. Read it first.
- `.mmd` edits made with pi's `edit` and `write` tools are validated
  automatically (in a temporary copy; nothing is sent). An edit you leave
  unsent is sent at the end of the run with an automatic note.
- Your job is the note. After editing, call `mmx_render({path, note})` with
  what changed and why. To reply without editing, call
  `mmx_note({path, text})`. To block for a reply inside a run, call
  `mmx_wait({path, timeoutSeconds})`.
- Suggest `/mmx open <path>` when the human should see or edit the picture
  in the local cockpit.

The sections below describe the same routine with these tools. The `mmx`
shell commands that remain (such as `mmx doctor`) run through `bash`.

If `mmx` is not on your PATH, install it first: follow `INSTALL.md` at the
repository root (https://github.com/Eastsidegunn/mmx/blob/main/INSTALL.md) —
it tells you how to probe your environment and install user-locally.

The human and agent edit the same `.mmd` file. `mmx render` writes `<stem>.svg`, `<stem>.diff.json`, and `<stem>.state.json`. The diff is the message for one turn; read it to learn what changed. Node IDs are stable names in the conversation.

When setup seems broken, run `mmx doctor <diagram.mmd>`.

## Turn routine

At the start of **every** turn, the extension collects the human's changes for you: before your run it asks mmx for each tracked diagram's unanswered human turns without waiting (without `mmx serve` running, this renders a direct edit of the file as the human's turn) and injects the human's unanswered turns as an `mmx-turn` message before your turn. Read them first. Each turn is injected once per session; `mmx_wait` still shows every unanswered turn.

A diagram is tracked once it is listed in `.pi/mmx.json`, opened with `/mmx open`, used with `mmx_render`, `mmx_note` or `mmx_wait`, or edited with pi's `edit` or `write`. No turn is injected for a diagram while you have an unsent edit to it.

Immediately after **every** `.mmd` edit you want the human to see, call:

```
mmx_render({path: "diagram.mmd", note: "Briefly describe the edit and reason"})
```

Edits made with pi's `edit` and `write` tools are validated automatically, and an edit you did not send is sent at the end of the run with an automatic note; your own note is better, so call `mmx_render` once the edit is done (several edits in one run can share one note). Edits to a tracked diagram made through `bash` or another tool are noticed after that tool call and treated the same way; an untracked diagram edited that way needs `mmx_render`.

`note` is recorded in diff.json and the turn log, and `mmx serve` shows it to the human. A non-empty `note` always makes a turn: if a hook (or `mmx serve`) already rendered the same bytes, the note arrives as a note-only turn (empty change sections) rather than being dropped; repeating the same note on unchanged bytes is a no-op. Without `note`, rendering unchanged bytes is a no-op that writes nothing. To reply without editing, use:

```
mmx_note({path: "diagram.mmd", text: "What you want to tell the human"})
```

`mmx_note` always makes a turn, as the agent; unrendered edits in the file become part of it. A parse error is reported like `mmx_render`'s, with line and column.

## Waiting for the human

In pi you rarely wait yourself: when the human presses Send in the cockpit, the extension delivers the turn as an `mmx-turn` message and starts a run (at most three automatic runs in a row; after that the turn waits for the next prompt). To block for a reply inside a run, call:

```
mmx_wait({path: "diagram.mmd", timeoutSeconds: 300})
```

- It returns one compact diff JSON line per human turn you have not answered yet (oldest first, same format as diff.json). Respond by editing the diagram and calling `mmx_render({path, note})`, or reply without editing via `mmx_note({path, text})`.
- `no human turn yet` means the timeout passed. Call it again, or stop. `timeoutSeconds: 0` does not block; it may take up to about half a second to settle and render a direct file edit that is still being written.
- It refuses while you have an unsent `.mmd` edit; call `mmx_render` first.

"Unanswered" means: human turns logged after the last non-human turn. With `mmx serve` running, the human speaks through the browser, and direct file edits are attributed to the agent (serve's poller renders them as `by: agent`). Without serve, `mmx wait` itself renders direct file edits (once the file is stable for two polls) as `by: human` and returns them.

## Turn log

Every committed turn (a successful render or a parse-error turn; never a no-op) appends one line to `<stem>.turns.jsonl`: `{"v":1,"at":<unix ms>,"by":..,"note":..,"source_sha256":..,"diff":{...}}`. When the file exceeds 2 MiB it is rewritten atomically to the newest 200 entries. Unparseable lines are skipped. `mmx serve` uses the log to show turns made by other processes and the full history; `mmx wait` reads it to find unanswered human turns. Do not edit it by hand.

## Read and respond

- `baseline: true` means no usable previous state. Change sections are empty; `stats` describes the first render.
- Added and removed nodes include their IDs, labels, and shapes. Added and removed edges include keys, endpoints, labels, and styles. Read these entries directly to understand the change; an ID rename appears as removal plus addition.
- `edges.changed` reports labels and solid/dotted/thick style changes. `direction` reports graph direction changes. `subgraphs` reports additions, removals, labels, membership, and direction changes.
- Read `source_hunks` for `classDef`, `style`, comments, and other source details. This is especially important when a non-flowchart warning says node/edge coverage is limited. `source_hunks: null` means there is no known previous source or the text is unchanged; `source_hunks_truncated: true` means only the first 400 hunk lines are present.
- `moved` reports relative node-center movement after subtracting `stats.global_shift`. The mean and max values measure remaining layout movement; mmx reports shifts but does not prevent them.
- `warnings` can flag a non-flowchart diagram (its node/edge diff is partial; `source_hunks` shows every text change), an empty flowchart, or recovery from corrupt/unsupported state.
- Quote labels containing brackets or pipes: `A["foo (bar"]`.
- `by` identifies the render caller, not proven edit authorship. A turn can carry no graph change and still contain a human `note`; that is the human asking a question; respond to it (edit the diagram, or answer with `mmx_note`).

See [diff-schema.md](references/diff-schema.md) for all diff and state fields.

### Known limitations

Sequence diagram message order is not modeled; changes are visible through `source_hunks` only. Layout positions are not stable across turns; `moved` reports movement but does not prevent it.

## Showing the diagram (one renderer, one picture)

When you display this diagram to the human — in an artifact, a web page, a
report — use the SVG that `mmx render` produced (`<stem>.svg`). Do NOT
re-render the same source with a different mermaid renderer (a native
```mermaid fence, mermaid.js, mermaid-cli): layouts differ between renderers,
so the human would see a different picture than the one this conversation's
diffs and coordinates describe. If the surrounding environment offers native
mermaid rendering, still prefer embedding mmx's SVG.

If the human should EDIT the diagram visually, suggest `/mmx open <path>`: it starts the local mmx cockpit for that diagram and opens it in the browser. The human's Send arrives as an `mmx-turn` message.

## Recover errors

In pi, `mmx_render` and `mmx_note` report exit 2 as a tool error with the kind, message, line, and column. The exit codes below are those of the `mmx` CLI underneath.

- Exit 0 means a successful render or no-op. No-op leaves all generated files untouched.
- Exit 2 means a repairable parse or UTF-8 encoding error. Read `diff.json.error` (`kind`, `message`, optional `line`, `column`, `candidates`), fix the `.mmd` file, and render again. SVG and state stay at their last valid versions.
- Exit 1 means an I/O, usage, path, or unsupported-format error; inspect stderr.

If the previous state is corrupt or unsupported, mmx backs it up as `<state>.corrupt` after a successful render, starts a baseline, and records a warning in diff.json. `mmx_render` reports this recovery turn as `baseline recorded`; if recovery is suspected, read `<stem>.diff.json` directly for the warning. Do not hand-edit generated state or diff files.

Use idiomatic Mermaid syntax. The strict parser differs from mermaid.js: in a sequence diagram with no participant declarations, it creates participants automatically; once any participant is declared, every participant must be declared. It may accept some text mermaid.js rejects. Exit 0 does not guarantee that a separate Mermaid renderer accepts the source.
